reasons: Cited paragraph 4(c) covers only cessation of Services, licence revocation and return/destruction of Confidential Information; no transition assistance, data export or deletion certification appears in the supplied text, so a 'missing' classification with an insert is appropriate rather than an over-flag of an acceptable fallback.

The inserted language tracks the playbook model wording closely (six months' transition assistance at then-current rates, machine-readable return within 30 days, certified deletion thereafter) and is placed in the termination section as the redline guidance directs.

'Notwithstanding subsection (iv)' correctly prevents the existing return-or-destroy election from letting Kubient unilaterally destroy our data, addressing the walk-away risk with a minimal, targeted edit.
Comment is concise, first-person plural, explains the change, cites the playbook position and offers the 90-day/30-day fallback; deterministic checks are consistent with the substance.
